A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CounterMath study. Their text, figures, tables and Appendices A–C support comparison; the appendices match apart from page and figure numbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, human validation of the automated judge, and fine-tuning experiments on CounterMath, GSM8K and MATH.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated models, additional benchmark results and model-output case studies.

M1.justification: The filtering, validation, rationale-refinement and supervised fine-tuning pipeline remains unchanged, including Appendix C's prompts. V2 specifies LoRA training, but v1 did not specify the parameter-update approach, so this establishes additional documentation rather than a changed method.

E1.justification: Table 3 extends actual out-of-distribution evaluation from GSM8K and MATH to OlympiadBench-Math, MMLU-college-Math and AIME 2024, substantially broadening competition and college-mathematics coverage. CounterMath and the training-data sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Deepseek-R1, Claude3.7-sonnet and Gemini2.5-pro, substantially updating the strongest evaluated comparators. Table 3 removes GPT-4o-2024-08-06 from the GSM8K/MATH comparison, although GPT-4o remains in Table 1.

E3.justification: The documented prompts, evaluation metrics, benchmark size and training-sample count remain unchanged. No revised split, budget or testing procedure is specified. The newly stated LoRA, hardware and learning-rate information does not establish a change to previously reported settings.

E4.justification: New Section 6.4 and Figure 7 add three qualitative cases examining correct judgments with irrelevant reasoning, judge acceptance of a non-reference counterexample, and an arithmetic error corrected after fine-tuning. Existing field-wise, token-efficiency, hint-prompt and human-validation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The 100-case human validation and its reporting practice are unchanged.

E6.justification: Shared table scores are unchanged, but the expanded Table 1 raises the best listed macro-F1 from o1-preview's 60.1 to Deepseek-R1's 80.7 through added models. Table 3 adds nine scores and removes GPT-4o's scores. Newly reported SFT results are 46.4, 80.0 and 30.0 on the three added benchmarks; its OlympiadBench score remains below the 72B baseline's 49.2.

T1.justification: Figure 7 adds explicit ring-theoretic counterexamples and a worked arithmetic derivation absent from v1. This is limited mathematical content rather than a new theoretical framework. Its purported R = {0} counterexample is incorrect because a = 0 belongs to N = {0}.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: CounterMath exposes conceptual-reasoning weaknesses, and training on 1,025 counterexample-oriented samples improves mathematical reasoning and generalization. The additional experiments support retained claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 newly interprets cases as demonstrating judgment–reasoning mismatches, successful evaluation of novel counterexamples and improved arithmetic consistency after training. The claimed judge-validation success is undermined by the displayed invalid counterexample. Existing explanations of field differences and limited-SFT shortcomings remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly discloses supervised LoRA training, two L20 48GB GPUs and a learning rate of 1.0e-5. The introduction adds a CounterMath repository link. Existing annotation details and appendix prompts are unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Wang et al. MMLU-Pro reference and source links for the newly evaluated models. The related-work discussion and positioning against drill-based learning, formal theorem proving and other conceptual-reasoning benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 adds a case-study subsection and acknowledgements, updates affiliation, correspondence and publication information, and makes localized edits to experimental descriptions.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel Figure 7, expands Table 3 from two to five benchmark columns and makes it span both columns, and compacts Table 1 to accommodate added rows. Existing figures are retained; the appendix annotation example is renumbered from Figure 7 to Figure 8.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical breadth through stronger comparators and additional generalization tests, and provides useful training details. However, new Figure 7 incorrectly presents R = {0} as a successful counterexample showing a does not belong to N, although a = 0 belongs to N = {0}. This undermines its added judge-validation argument. The useful additions and material new validity error leave the net quality direction uncertain.
